keyFindings.text: **P0 — 005's memory entry line format is unspecified: five fields are named, the serialization is not.** The plan says `memory.ts` "owns the entry line, its five fields, the four types, the three bounds, the parser, the renderer" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/005-memory/plan.md:60], and REQ-001 names type, date, actor, source and text [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/005-memory/spec.md:157], but no literal example line, delimiter, escaping rule for a `|` or a newline, or `--forget` index rule appears in spec, plan or tasks. Two builders produce two incompatible files, and the acceptance criteria only test round-trip, so both pass. Closing artifact: `contracts/memory-entry.md` with one literal example line, the delimiter, the escaping rule, the index rule, and the 60-entry/3,600-byte/400-character bound restated as a table.

**P0 — No schema file or contract document exists anywhere in the packet, so every record shape is prose in a REQ table and no builder can check a field name against a single source.** The packet holds fourteen phase folders and zero `*.schema.json` files; the only JSON under `specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/` is research state (`deep-research-config.json`, `findings-registry.json`, `frontier-nodes.jsonl`). The nearest thing to a contract is 003's fixture, described as "the copy of every `--json` contract the screen reads" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/006-hardening-and-proof/plan.md:122]. Closing artifact: a packet-level `contracts/` folder with one JSON Schema per record (needs-you item, answer, run record, run summary, activity payload, inbox payload, routines payload, conversation message, grant, memory entry, routine state) plus a `contracts/README.md` index naming the owning phase per file. Because 001, 002, 005, 006, 009 and 010 all add fields to the same three records, the folder belongs to a new cross-cutting phase (`015-contracts-and-schemas`) that lands before 001, not to any one child.

**P1 — 001 adds `by` and `scope` to the answer object but never states what an answer written before the phase reads as, while the run record's null rule is stated twice.** `NeedsYouAnswer` is `{text, answeredAt}` today [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/needs-you.ts:25-28] and `validateNeedsYouItem` requires `answer.text` and `answer.answeredAt` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/needs-you.ts:117-120]. 001 states the null rule for `actor` and `answeredBy` on the run record [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:193] and for the index summary [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:192], but REQ-004 and REQ-010 say only that the answer "records" `by` and `scope` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:158] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:166]. A builder must decide whether a required `by` refuses every existing item file. Closing artifact: one nullability sentence in 001 REQ-004 plus a `needs-you.vitest.ts` row for a pre-phase answer, and the answer schema in `contracts/`.

**P1 — 002's `until` observation on the run record is named but not shaped.** The Files to Change row says only "Carry the optional `until` observation on the record" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/002-routine-layer/spec.md:135], while the same phase specifies the `until_check` exit semantics in REQ-004 [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/002-routine-layer/spec.md:161]. The record field list (`met`, `at`, `exitClass`, `command`?) is left to the builder, and `bots routines` reads `untilMetAt` from the state file rather than the record, so the record field has no reader and no shape. Closing artifact: the run-record schema in `contracts/` with the `until` object's fields, or a decision to drop the field because the state file already carries the outcome.

**P1 — 002's routine state file has three named fields and no schema.** `recordUntilOutcome` writes `untilMetAt`, `evaluateFatigue` records `fatiguedAt` and the item id [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/002-routine-layer/plan.md:62], but the file's version key, its `botId`, the failure-streak field name, the absent-file default and the write atomicity are all unstated. `bots routines` reads "the identity's routine state files" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/002-routine-layer/plan.md:73], so the reader and the writer must agree on a shape nobody wrote down. Closing artifact: `contracts/routine-state.schema.json` plus a `routine-state.vitest.ts` row for an absent file and a file written by an older shape.

**P1 — Three `--json` verbs use three envelope conventions and no rule picks one.** `bots activity --json` prints `{"groups":[]}` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:229], `bots chat --json` prints "the messages as a JSON array" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/010-conversations/spec.md:158], and `bots routines --json` names its row fields but never says whether the payload is an array or an object [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/002-routine-layer/spec.md:178]. A builder of 002 must guess, and 003's fixture then encodes the guess. Closing artifact: `contracts/json-envelope.md` with one rule (object with a named collection key, or array) applied to every verb, and the three payload schemas beside it.

**P2 — The needs-you item lifecycle is a derived state with no transition table.** `NeedsYouState` is `open | answered | expired` and is never stored [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/needs-you.ts:47] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/needs-you.ts:90-92]; 001 prints it [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:153], 006 adds the second-answer refusal `item-answered-differently` and the guarded write [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/006-approval-grants/spec.md:170] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/006-approval-grants/spec.md:171], and 005 adds a review seam that settles an item without a resume [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/005-memory/spec.md:167]. The transition table is split across three phases and no doc states who writes `answeredAt`, when `expired` is computed, or what a second answer does on each kind. Closing artifact: `contracts/item-lifecycle.md` with the transition table and the writer per transition.

**P0 — 011 is the packet's largest phase and has no children, so one builder must design the adapter contract, the link and roster, the approval index, the durable queue and five wire protocols in a single pass.** It lists 27 files to change, nine new runtime modules, five transports and seven new test files [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:140-170], and its spec is 311 lines against 003's 279 — yet 003 is a phase parent with six children and 011 is a leaf [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:157]. Closing artifact: make 011 a phase parent with six children — `001-shared-adapter-and-contract` (`channel.ts`, the message model, the capability table, the unsupported rule, `channels/config.json`), `002-identity-link-and-roster` (`channel-link.ts`, the pairing code, the lockout, `operators.json`, the roster check in `answer.ts`), `003-approval-index-and-queue` (`channel-approval.ts`, `channel-queue.ts`, the reply grammar, the backoff table), `004-telegram-and-slack` (the two no-public-URL transports with native buttons), `005-signal-and-whatsapp` (the local daemon and the signed webhook, both on the numbered grammar), `006-conformance-and-hardening` (the five conformance rules, the fake transport, the notices, the operator runbook).

**P1 — `declaredCapabilities` has no vocabulary: the contract names the member but never the capability names a transport declares, so the `unsupported` rule has nothing to test against.** REQ-001 fixes the six contract members and the `unsupported` result shape [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:183], and the plan says the table is what the conformance suite checks [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/plan.md:66], but no list of capability keys (`send`, `edit`, `react`, `buttons`, `attachments`, `threads`, `typing`?) appears anywhere. Closing artifact: a capability table in `contracts/channel-adapter.md` with one row per capability and one column per transport, which is also the conformance fixture's input.

**P1 — REQ-017 promises five conformance rules and enumerates two, so a builder invents three of five.** The requirement reads "Five conformance rules run as fixture tests on a fake transport: an undeclared operation returns `unsupported` and reaches no platform; a declared one returns no provider error and produces one matching wire observation with a receipt" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:204], and the test file is described only as "the five conformance rules on a fake transport" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:159]. Closing artifact: the five rules enumerated in `contracts/channel-adapter.md` (the two stated plus, by the reference's own shape, an idempotency-key replay rule, a chunk-limit rule and a token-redaction rule), each with its fixture.

**P1 — The durable queue entry has no field list.** REQ-013 fixes the semantics (write before I/O, `unknown` never retried, backoff 0/5/25/120/600 s) [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:195] and the plan names the reference's queue and policy files [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/plan.md:70], but the entry's fields (`id`, `channel`, `conversation`, `body`, `attempts`, `nextAttemptAt`, `state`, `createdAt`?) are unstated, and `bots channel list` prints "queue depth from `queue/`" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:206], so the reader depends on a shape nobody wrote. Closing artifact: `contracts/channel-queue.schema.json` with the state enum and the backoff table as data.

**P1 — The link record has no field list and no file name in Files to Change.** REQ-003 says the link "records both that actor and the provider-asserted sender id" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:185], and `links.json` appears only in the Data Flow and in REQ-019/REQ-023 [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/plan.md:76] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:206], never in the Files to Change table, which names only `channel-link.ts`. A builder must invent the file name, the key (chat id? channel plus chat id?), the field names and the unlink removal rule. Closing artifact: `contracts/channel-link.schema.json` plus one Files to Change row for `links.json` under `state-root.ts`.

**P1 — The per-transport operator prerequisites are a dependency table, not a runbook.** The table names the four prerequisites (a bot token, a Slack app-level token with Socket Mode, a registered Signal number with a local daemon, a public HTTPS URL plus a Meta business account) [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:236-242], but no artifact gives the exact scopes, events and webhook fields an operator must set. `bots-run/references/messaging-channels.md` is already in Files to Change [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:167], so the closing artifact is a per-channel setup checklist in that file: Telegram `allowed_updates` of `message` and `callback_query`, Slack `connections:write` plus `chat:write` and the `block_actions` interaction, Signal `signal-cli daemon --http` on localhost, WhatsApp `messages` webhook field plus the app secret for `X-Hub-Signature-256`.

**P2 — The approval index file's key structure is unstated while its fields are listed.** REQ-006 lists the entry's fields (action id, item id, channel, conversation, choices, `expiresAt`) and the expiry removal rule [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:188], but not whether the file is a map keyed by action id or an array, which decides the lookup cost and the concurrent-write rule. Closing artifact: one line in `contracts/channel-approval.schema.json`.

**P0 — The README's allowed-direction rule is already false in the code it governs, and 011 adds a fourth violation, so a builder cannot tell whether to follow the rule or the code.** The rule reads "a contracts module imports no `lib/` module outside its own group" [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/README.md:39], but `answer.ts` — a contracts-and-state module — imports `dispatch.js`, `request-queue.js` and `runner.js` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/answer.ts:22-27], three modules outside its group. 011 REQ-021 then adds a roster check to `answer.ts` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:208], which would import `channel-link.ts` as a fourth. Closing artifact: restate the rule as the layering the code actually has (or invert the roster check behind an injected predicate passed by the caller), and add a `rg` check to the phase's verification so the rule cannot drift again.

keyFindings.text: **P1 — `bots chat --json` as a bare array is the one verb that breaks the precedent, and 003's chat pane reads it, so changing it later breaks the screen.** 010 REQ-006 fixes the array [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/010-conversations/spec.md:158] and REQ-008 makes the chat pane read that payload [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/010-conversations/spec.md:160], while 003's fixture is the copy of every `--json` contract the screen reads [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/006-hardening-and-proof/plan.md:122]. Closing artifact: change 010 REQ-006 to `{"messages": [...]}` before 003's fixture is written, and record the change in 010's decision record.

**P1 — No phase states the stdout/stderr split for a `--json` verb, though the existing verb already implements it.** `bots status --json` sends rebuild progress to stderr and the document to stdout, so a caller can parse stdout unconditionally [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/bots.cjs:376-388]. The new verbs (`activity`, `inbox`, `routines`, `chat`, `channel list`) state no such rule, so a builder may print a warning to stdout and break every parser. Closing artifact: one rule in `contracts/json-envelope.md` — "with `--json`, stdout carries only the JSON document and every human line goes to stderr" — plus one test per verb.

**P1 — The packet has no envelope rule, and the three new verbs disagree: `activity` prints an object, `chat` prints a bare array, and `routines` prints neither by name.** `bots activity --json` prints `{"groups":[]}` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:229], `bots chat --json` prints "the messages as a JSON array" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/010-conversations/spec.md:158], and `bots routines --json` names its row fields without an envelope [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/002-routine-layer/spec.md:178]. Closing artifact: `contracts/json-envelope.md` with one rule and one schema per verb.

**P1 — The precedent is unambiguous and it is the object envelope: `bots status --json` prints the whole `StatusReport` object with named keys, never a bare array.** The verb writes `JSON.stringify(report.value, null, 2)` [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/bots.cjs:386-388], and `StatusReport` is `{indexPath, builtAt, stale, staleIdentities, rows, duplicateRoots, notes}` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/status.ts:103-114]. So the rule the packet should adopt is "one object with named keys; a collection is a named key", which makes `activity`'s `{groups: []}` correct and `chat`'s bare array the one violation. Closing artifact: the rule stated in `contracts/json-envelope.md` with `status` cited as the precedent.

**P2 — Two different `state` vocabularies ship in one packet: an item's `state` is `open|answered|expired` and an activity row's `state` is one of the seven group ids.** 001 REQ-003 fixes the item vocabulary [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:153] and REQ-002 fixes the row vocabulary as "one of the seven group ids" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:152], so a reader that handles both payloads sees one key name with two meanings. Closing artifact: rename the activity row field to `group` in 001 REQ-002, or state both vocabularies side by side in `contracts/json-envelope.md`.

keyFindings.text: **P1 — no phase owns the exit-code convention.** `EXIT_CODES` at `runner.ts:113-120` is a frozen six-value object — `completed` 0, `runFailure` 1, `usage` 2, `recursionGuard` 3, `refused` 4, `awaitingDecision` 5 — and `bots-run/references/run-queue-and-answer.md:15` names it as the table a reader checks. Zero of the 14 phase specs cite `EXIT_CODES`; each restates a bare number. keyFindings.text: **P1 — no phase states which of its refusals are pre-dispatch and which are post-dispatch.** `RunExit.refusal` is documented as "Present when the run was refused before dispatch, so a refusal never reads as a failure" (`run-record.ts:137-138`), and `REFUSAL_CAUSES` mixes both kinds — `body-secret` is pre-dispatch, `resume-posture-changed` happens at resume. ruledOutDirections.text: Looking for a migration section: every phase's complexity table asserts "no migration" or "no data migration" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:244] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/005-memory/spec.md:250], so the packet has no migration artifact to extend; the nullability rules are the migration story and they are incomplete for the answer object.

Reading the phase `tasks.md` files for the missing shapes: they carry verify commands (`rg -n 'MEMORY_LIMITS|parseMemory|renderMemory'`) rather than field lists, so they confirm a symbol exists and never its shape. Checked 005's tasks T007-T010 and 002's T001-T006.
Searching for a `contracts/` or `schemas/` folder under the packet root returns nothing, so there is no partial artifact to extend.

The `crates/bots-tui/tests/fixtures/bots` contract gap is already closed in the packet: 001's affected-surfaces table marks the fixture "not this phase's" and asserts payloads through `bots ... --json` instead [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/plan.md:92], and 003's child 006 enumerates the four payloads the fixture carries [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/006-hardening-and-proof/plan.md:122]. Do not re-raise it as a missing Modify row; the remaining gap is that the payload shapes themselves have no schema file (finding 1).

Treating the parent phase map's "Depends on" column as the interface contract: it names one dependency per phase in prose ("001, whose run records carry the fields") and no field, so it cannot close a schema gap [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:151-166].
Looking for a conformance fixture list in `tasks.md`: the tasks name the test files and their verify commands, not the rules.

Reading the acceptance-criteria file for the missing shapes: it asserts behavior per requirement and names no field, so it cannot close a schema gap. Checked 011's AC rows for REQ-001, REQ-006 and REQ-017.

The adapter contract itself is not a gap: REQ-001 and REQ-002 give the six members and the four message shapes with every field [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:183-184], so the contract is deeper than 001's or 005's. Do not re-raise it; the gap is the capability vocabulary and the conformance rules, not the interface.

The reference-code question is already answered inside the phase: the plan cites `tinychannels-main`'s `adapter.rs`, `envelope.rs`, `intent.rs`, `receipt.rs`, `error.rs`, `delivery/queue.rs`, `delivery/policy.rs`, `security/mod.rs` and `bus/config.rs`, and states the reference is GPL-3.0 so it is design only [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/plan.md:66-72]. A child split should keep those citations per child rather than re-deriving them.

Treating the plan's Data Flow as the contract: it names `links.json`, `approvals.json` and `queue/` in passing [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/plan.md:76] but gives no field, so it locates the files without specifying them.

002's own depth is not the gap here: its block rules, floor, fatigue count and refusal names are specified to the field level [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/002-routine-layer/spec.md:153-181]; the gaps iteration 1 found (state file, `until` observation) are the only ones, so 002 needs no child either.

Concluding that 004 needs a child: it lists 12 files, nine requirements, the exact prompt line text, the null-branch variant and a design-reference per requirement [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/004-computer-exposure/spec.md:150-180], so it is the packet's best example of a one-shot-ready small phase. It needs the shared contracts, not children.
Looking for a per-phase "Interfaces" section: the Level 2 template has no such anchor, so the offered and consumed interfaces are only ever prose inside Scope and Requirements.

The README is not useless: its package topology and module table are the right shape for the target-state doc, so the closing artifact is an extension of that file plus a `contracts/` copy, not a new invention.

Treating the parent spec's phase map as the architecture doc: it names one dependency per phase and no module, group or edge [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:151-166].

Assuming the pretty-print indentation is part of the contract: `status` uses `null, 2` [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/bots.cjs:387], but no test compares exact whitespace, so indentation is a style choice rather than a contract and is not raised as a gap.
Looking for an envelope rule in the parent spec: the phase map names no payload and no verb [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:151-166].

The `--json` flag parsing itself is not a gap: `json` is already in `FLAG_OPTIONS` and `STATUS_OPTIONS` [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/bots.cjs:59-62], so a new verb inherits the flag with no parser change. The gap is the payload, not the flag.

Treating `bots status --json` as a special case because it prints a report rather than a list: the report is the only precedent the packet has, and its shape (object with a named collection key) is exactly what `activity` already follows, so it generalizes.
009's addition is a value rather than a key, so it does not widen the array; only 001, 005, 006 and 010 do.
Looking for a generated schema of the item: no schema file exists (iteration 1), so the table is the only ownership artifact.

Re-raising the `kind` collision as an unknown: the prior research already found it and the parent's Shared Records table already assigns the values to 005 [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/research/research.md:577], so the open part is the nested `grants.kind`, not the top-level one.
The `unknown-key` refusal is not the problem: it is the mechanism that makes the closed list safe, and it works. The problem is that five phases edit the list without one target.
Treating the landing order as the fix: the phases land 001, 005, 006, 009, 010 in numeric order, but order cannot reconcile two vocabularies or supply a missing key list.
Looking for an existing lock helper to cite: the runtime has the atomic-rename convention but no exported lock, so 008 would have to introduce one or state that last-writer-wins is accepted.

Reading 007 as under-planned. It names its refusals (`apps-unknown-server`, `apps-unenforceable`), its env key (`UTCP_CONFIG_FILE` through `dispatchEnvKeys`), its filtered-config write and its worktree-restore-after-exit rule. It is the second-best-planned phase in the packet after 004, and needs no child.

Searching for a name grammar in the reference code to adopt by citation: rakazo's `bot-secrets.md:35` is cited for the 16,384 bound only, and the packet never cites it for the grammar. Adopting one would be a design decision the phase does not authorize.
Treating 008 as needing a phase parent. Its 19 files and 15 requirements are one coherent store plus one injection path; the gaps above are additions to the existing documents, not a split.

Looking for a `kind` field on `NeedsYouItem` today: `needs-you.ts:29-48` has no such field and `ITEM_KEYS` does not list it, so 005's REQ-009 is what introduces it. That confirms the field is 005's to define and makes finding 3 a contradiction between two phases rather than a missing field.
Looking for a skill-name grammar in `bot-check.cjs` to cite: the checker has no name-grammar helper, so 009 has nothing to reuse.

Reading 009 as needing a phase parent. Its 25 files are one loader plus one proposal path, and its caps, overflow rule, wrapper format and digest chain are all pinned. The gaps are four additions to the existing documents.

Reading 012 as under-planned. It has a 33-row inventory with a requirement citation per row, a package validator as its gate, a single writer for the run folder (`record-playbook-run.cjs`), a FAIL-handling requirement, a SKIP rule for a missing channel account, and a wave plan. It needs no child phase; it needs two rules added (findings 6 and 8).
Looking for 013's report folders in 014's inputs: 014's dependency list is five bullets and none names them, which is what makes finding 1 a boundary gap rather than a wording quibble.
Looking for a host-capacity rule in the fan-out contract: the plan's fallback order covers which executor to prefer, not what to do when one is absent.
Reading 013 as needing a child phase. It is two command runs plus a fix pass; its problem is where the evidence lands, not how much design it needs.

Reading 014 as under-planned. It is the deepest plan in the packet: five named dimensions mapped onto four canonical ids, a five-part stop rule with the frontier veto and the strongest-restriction verdict, a roster with per-kind effort and enforced allowlists, a fallback order, a file-partitioned fix pass, and a measured test floor. Its gaps are boundary rules, not design.
Treating 014's "at least 381 tests" as a gap. The number is a floor measured before the build, so a larger suite still passes.

Looking for a packet-level catalogue file: `grep -rln "refusal catalogue|error catalogue|refusal table|exit-code table"` over the packet returns nothing, so the vocabulary lives only in `runner.ts` and in each phase's prose.
Looking for a state-root or record version field: neither `state-root.ts` nor `run-record.ts` has one, and only 001 mentions "record version" at all, in an unrelated sense.
Reading the packet as having no refusal discipline. It has a typed registry, a frozen exit-code object and a documented table; the gap is that no phase document points at any of them.
Treating concurrency as unowned. 002, 005, 006, 010 and 011 each state their queue and lease rules in detail; the gap is the shared-file writers, not the queue owners.
Treating migration as entirely absent. 006's risk row and 008's "read a missing field as a default" are real compatibility rules; they are just not a migration story.
Looking for a phase whose size alone justifies a split: 009 at 25 files and 001 and 002 at 24 are large but each is one module family, and iteration 7 already ruled out a parent for 009.
Looking for design artifacts outside 003: the grep over all 28 spec and plan files returns one match, so there is nothing to consolidate — the gap is total for 010 and 011.
Making 003's six-child shape the template for every phase. 003 is a Level 3 phase with a screen to draw; 004, 007, 013 and 014 are smaller than 003's first child and would be damaged by a split.
Making 008, 009 or 010 a parent. Each is one coherent module plus one seam; their gaps are missing contract text, not missing decomposition.
Treating the contract document as a fifteenth phase. It is an artifact the existing phases cite, not a build step, and giving it a phase would put a document in the build order.
